statement: Show that there are only finitely many solutions to \(\dfrac{1}{a} + \dfrac{1}{b} + \dfrac{1}{c} = \dfrac{1}{1983}\) in positive integers.

An equilateral triangle \(ABC\) has side \(a\). A square is constructed on the outside of each side. A right regular pyramid with sloping edge \(a\) is placed on each square, then rotated about the corresponding side of the triangle until all three apexes meet at a common point above the triangle. Show that the other vertices of the bases of the pyramids (other than the triangle's vertices) form a regular hexagon.
Show that \(1 + \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{3} + \cdots + \dfrac{1}{n}\) is not an integer for \(n > 1\).
Show that it is possible to color each point of a circle red or blue so that no right-angled triangle inscribed in the circle has all three vertices the same color.
Show that \(1 \leq n^{1/n} \leq 2\) for all positive integers \(n\). Find the smallest \(k\) such that \(1 \leq n^{1/n} \leq k\) for all positive integers \(n\).
Show that the maximum number of unit spheres that can be placed touching a fixed unit sphere, with no two having a common interior point, is between \(12\) and \(14\).
